notes: Useful as primary physiological support for salt adaptation, but not enough by itself to define a stable optimum for the curated table.

notes: Promoted to the exploratory algae table as a species-level but quantitatively supported halophilic alga.

key_evidence: Maximum specific growth rate was highest at 35 C in 35 PPT marine salts, with similarly strong growth at 50 PPT and tolerance up to 100 PPT.
notes: Promoted to the exploratory algae table as a saline-adapted alga; 35 PPT marine salts were treated as approximately seawater-equivalent salinity.

key_evidence: P. renovo exhibits broad salinity tolerance with growth at 107.5 g/L salinity and thermotolerance up to 40 C; later screening data identify 35 PSU as the optimum salinity and 35 C as the peak-growth temperature.
notes: Promoted to the exploratory algae table using the primary strain paper plus later screening data specifying the optimum salinity of 35 PSU.

key_evidence: Maximum specific growth rate of Picochlorum renovo NREL 39-A8 was reported as a function of salinity, with the temperature screen carried out at the optimum salinity of 35 PSU.
notes: Supports the curated P. renovo row by providing the explicit optimum salinity used in the temperature-growth screen.

notes: Promoted to the exploratory algae table as a species-level halophilic alga with a direct optimum-growth value from a primary paper.
